title: Monoclonal antibodies
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point covers the natural adaptive immune response (B cells making antibodies and T cells killing infected cells), while the new point is about lab-made monoclonal antibodies and their use in treating cancer and autoimmune disease, which is a different idea.

draft.title: Monoclonal antibodies
card: An antibody is a protein that binds to one specific antigen. Monoclonal antibodies are antibodies made in the lab that are all identical and all target the same antigen.
They are made by a clone of one B cell. A B cell that makes the wanted antibody is joined with a cancerous cell that divides without limit. The joined cell makes large amounts of one antibody.
For cancer, a monoclonal antibody can bind to an antigen on the surface of cancer cells. This can mark the cells for destruction or block signals that make them divide.
For autoimmune diseases, the immune system attacks the body's own cells. A monoclonal antibody can bind to a signalling molecule involved in that attack and reduce the damage.
draft.remember: One antigen, one antibody type, made in bulk to treat disease.

a.q: Why are monoclonal antibodies useful as a targeted treatment?
opts: Each one binds to a single specific antigen
Each one binds to many different antigens
Each one is made by many different B cells
Each one destroys any cell it meets
a.why: All the antibodies in a batch are identical, so they bind to the same antigen and not to other molecules. Antibodies that bind many antigens, or destroy any cell, would not be targeted.
a.clue: Think about what monoclonal tells you about the antibodies.

b.q: A drug company wants a treatment that acts only on cells carrying antigen X, found on a patient's cancer cells. What should it make?
opts: Monoclonal antibodies that bind antigen X
Monoclonal antibodies that bind any surface antigen
Antibodies from many B cells that bind antigen Y
Cancerous cells that divide without limit
b.why: Antibodies that bind antigen X will attach to the cancer cells carrying it. Antibodies for any antigen, or for antigen Y, would not be matched to those cells. The dividing cells are only part of how the antibodies are made.
b.clue: Match the antibody to the antigen on the target cells.

a.best: Each one binds to a single specific antigen

b.best: Monoclonal antibodies that bind antigen X
